text: According to Locke, what does personal identity over time consist in?
choices: The continuity of consciousness, in particular the extension of memory back to past thoughts and actions
The continuity of the same immaterial soul-substance, whatever consciousness it happens to carry
The biological continuity of the same living human organism
The coherence of the story one tells to make one's life intelligible as a whole
explanation: Locke holds that identity follows consciousness — 'as far as this consciousness can be extended backwards' — so it consists in memory continuity, not sameness of substance. The prince-and-cobbler case shows he rejects the soul-substance criterion; the organism criterion is Olson's later animalism; and the life-story criterion is MacIntyre and Ricoeur's narrative identity. Only memory continuity is Locke's view.
